flawed_step: Lines 0116–0130 incorrectly infer that an (s,t)-flow has no inflow into s, and hence identify its value with gross outflow from s. In general, flow value is net outflow, so incoming-edge terms must be included.
counterexample: Let the network have unit-capacity edges s→a, a→b, b→s, and s→t. Let f send one unit around s→a→b→s and zero to t; let g send one unit on s→t and zero elsewhere. Then |g|=1>|f|=0, but line 0118 claims |f|=Σ_y f(s,y)=1, which is false because f also has one unit entering s.
assessment_summary: The capacity and intermediate-vertex conservation arguments can be read coherently, but the value argument makes an unjustified assumption that the source has no incoming flow. The problem statement supplies no such restriction, so the proof as written is incomplete.
